Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Coverage and verification procedure:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, their approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps,
and uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts you emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
For composite objects, match the overall silhouette and the distribution of occupied space
and gaps before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their
parent and nearby objects from the reference. A correct outer bounding box alone does not
ensure the correct internal density, component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these
parameters explicit so that a later revision can change them without rebuilding the design.

Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction.
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, silhouette, internal gaps, relative sizes, overlaps and image
bounds. Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If many objects share
a displacement or scale error, consider camera/framing; if a discrepancy is local, consider
that object's parameters. Neither pattern proves a unique cause. Preserve matching objects
and their editable hierarchy while correcting the supported discrepancies. Do not impose
one fixed density, camera, object count or parameter adjustment across different inputs.
An isolated-object view, if supplied, can clarify membership and silhouette, but its full-image
score is not evidence that removing the rest of the scene improves the reconstruction.
Keep unresolved mappings and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. A short
Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a
compact complete first build so that realization and the runner's render can finish with
time for review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade
this budget. Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. In this implementation, each ball, rod and box emits a separate
mesh and marker; a fillet_box can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits
2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands
also incur mesh creation and modifier work. Count these expansions, not just named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes across the whole scene, as a planning
heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail
according to visible pixel size, silhouette and gaps. If the estimate reaches thousands,
simplify repeated microstructure before execution while retaining every inventory object
and its meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials
and restrained procedural shading; retain geometric detail that changes visible contours,
openings or occlusions. Avoid nested per-element decoration below the image resolution.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths for visible curves, concentrating points at bends.
Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to approximate one hollow shape; use a small
number of appropriate SceneAct solids and cutters, preserving the visible opening. Prefer
boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for parts whose
rounded edges matter. Keep a small reusable material palette for each surface family rather
than generating a distinct random color and material for every tiny primitive. Keep parent
assets, semantic child parts, and support relations intact during simplification.
If execution times out without an image, report that completion failed and the bottleneck
is unknown unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts,
Boolean operations and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera,
coverage or appearance defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution
and rendered-image verification; simplification alone is not evidence of success.

Execution verification:
realize(scene) clears Blender to an empty factory scene. Configure the world, camera,
lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting
world nodes, use this initialization after realize:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:
        sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
    sc.world.use_nodes = True
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
    if background is None:
        background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails, use the actual traceback
to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies no rendered visual
feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Preserve
explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification when no successful render exists.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

Reconstruct this RGB image. Match its camera and framing. Image dimensions: 512 x 341. Budget: {'model_calls': 4, 'executions': 3, 'seconds': 3599.9994732141495}
Before writing the complete program, choose a small set of visible image anchors distributed across foreground, main subject and background. Record their approximate normalized positions or bounds in program comments, together with a few dominant edge directions and overlaps. Use the original image aspect throughout. These are visual estimates, not ground-truth calibration. Parameterize camera pose, target and lens separately from major asset dimensions and positions. Prioritize the contours and large light/dark regions that occupy the image; fine detail cannot repair incorrect framing or a wrong silhouette.
Use a small numerical projection check before committing camera changes. Choose a few
explicit world-space landmarks corresponding to reference points you can actually identify:
for example a window corner, a furniture top corner and a foreground contour endpoint.
Record reference estimates separately from computed projections. Use points on geometry,
not an EMPTY's origin or a whole-room bounding box. Include foreground and background.
After realize and set_view, update Blender's view layer. For a world point p, project using:
    from mathutils import Vector
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    cam = sc.camera
    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
    projection = cam.calc_matrix_camera(dg, x=sc.render.resolution_x,
        y=sc.render.resolution_y, scale_x=sc.render.pixel_aspect_x,
        scale_y=sc.render.pixel_aspect_y)
    clip = projection @ cam.matrix_world.inverted() @ Vector((*p, 1.0))
    uv = None if clip.w <= 1e-8 else (
        .5 * (clip.x / clip.w + 1), .5 * (1 - clip.y / clip.w))
Use the original image aspect for these calculations and the final camera. Coordinates
are x right and y down. Print a compact reference-versus-projected landmark table in
execution output. This requires no render. Projection checks do not establish visibility,
silhouette, material appearance or correct hidden geometry.
When changing camera aim, position or lens, compute the same landmark projections before
and after a small trial change to verify the direction rather than guessing. Restore a
trial that moves the selected landmarks the wrong way. With a fixed camera position,
aiming upward generally moves stationary scene features downward in the image. Lens
changes scale positions about the principal point; moving the camera changes foreground
and background differently. Do not compensate a local dimension or placement error by
moving every matching background feature. Keep this check small: a few landmarks and
candidate parameter adjustments, not a large search. Do not force uncertain point
correspondences or optimize hidden bounds. The complete rendered view remains the final
check of crops, occlusions, silhouettes and broad appearance.

```python
# Cleanroom packaging line reconstruction.
# Reference inventory and visual anchors, normalized image coordinates (x right, y down):
# - Foreground operator: roughly (0.17, 0.00)-(0.68, 1.00); white coat, hairnet,
#   side-profile face, raised arm reaching the HMI. Lower body is partly occluded.
# - Background operator: (0.00, 0.15)-(0.22, 1.00); white coat, hairnet, glasses,
#   hands held at waist. Legs and body partly cropped/occluded.
# - HMI: (0.62, 0.06)-(0.80, 0.47), tall tilted pale screen with metal rim;
#   its lower edge overlaps the machine and its left edge meets the operator's hand.
# - Packaging line: (0.43, 0.37)-(1.00, 1.00); dark mechanical center, metal frames,
#   transparent guards, pale belt running toward the foreground at lower right.
# - Conveyor: near end around (0.56, 0.82)-(0.84, 1.00), recedes toward (0.53, 0.68).
# - Room: bright ceiling panels across top and upper left, pale back/right walls,
#   very little floor visible. Horizontal architectural edges recede to the right.
# Major edge directions: HMI sides slope up to the right; belt sides converge toward
# the rear; ceiling grid and guard rails recede toward the center of the image.
# Uncertain: machine internals behind the operator and reflective guard, concealed
# legs, and exact products on the belt. Their geometry is kept schematic.
#
# Approximate expanded primitive count: room 35; machine and guard 100; HMI 12;
# two people 42; ceiling lights 15; total about 205 meshes. No fillet boxes,
# Boolean operations, or dense tube paths are used.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector

# Independent camera parameters and scene proportions, in meters.
CAMERA_POS = (3.55, -6.7, 2.35)
CAMERA_TARGET = (0.02, 1.65, 1.67)
CAMERA_LENS = 37
ROOM_W, ROOM_D, ROOM_H = 8.0, 12.0, 3.65
LINE_X = 1.05
BELT_WIDTH = 1.02
BELT_FRONT, BELT_BACK, BELT_Z = -1.8, 4.4, 0.91

scene = Scene("Cleanroom packaging line")
white = (0.82, 0.91, 0.89)
wall = (0.70, 0.82, 0.80)
floor = (0.61, 0.74, 0.72)
steel = (0.48, 0.59, 0.59)
darksteel = (0.12, 0.20, 0.20)
black = (0.035, 0.065, 0.065)
belt = (0.83, 0.90, 0.85)
glass = (0.54, 0.80, 0.79)
skin = (0.73, 0.51, 0.40)
hairnet = (0.64, 0.81, 0.79)
screen = (0.79, 0.94, 0.93)

def add_box(parent, name, size, center, color, opacity=1):
    parent.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color, opacity=opacity))

def add_rod(parent, name, a, b, radius, color):
    parent.include(name, rod(radius=radius, start=a, end=b, color=color))

def ellipsoid(parent, name, center, scale, color):
    obj = ball(1, center=center, color=color)
    obj.resize(scale, pivot=center)
    parent.include(name, obj)

# Room is deliberately open on the camera side.
room = Asset("Cleanroom architecture")
add_box(room, "floor", (ROOM_W, ROOM_D, .10), (0, 2, -.08), floor)
add_box(room, "back wall", (ROOM_W, .10, ROOM_H), (0, 7.0, ROOM_H/2), wall)
add_box(room, "right wall", (.10, ROOM_D, ROOM_H), (3.95, 2, ROOM_H/2), (0.75, .86, .84))
add_box(room, "ceiling", (ROOM_W, ROOM_D, .10), (0, 2, ROOM_H), (.77, .87, .85))
# A thin ceiling grid and luminous recessed panels define the room depth.
for x in (-3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3):
    add_box(room, "ceiling longitudinal %.1f" % x, (.025, 11.8, .018),
            (x, 2, ROOM_H-.065), (.59, .72, .70))
for y in (-2, 0, 2, 4, 6):
    add_box(room, "ceiling cross %.1f" % y, (7.9, .025, .018),
            (0, y, ROOM_H-.065), (.59, .72, .70))
for x in (-2.25, -.75, .75, 2.25):
    for y in (-1, 1, 3, 5):
        add_box(room, "recessed light %.1f %.1f" % (x, y), (1.12, 1.18, .022),
                (x, y, ROOM_H-.075), (1.0, 1.0, .97))
# restrained floor seams
for x in (-3, -1, 1, 3):
    add_box(room, "floor seam x %.1f" % x, (.012, 11.7, .004), (x, 2, -.026), (.48, .64, .62))
for y in (-2, 0, 2, 4, 6):
    add_box(room, "floor seam y %.1f" % y, (7.9, .012, .004), (0, y, -.025), (.48, .64, .62))
scene.include("room", room)

machine = Asset("Stainless packaging machine")
# Main lower casing and supporting frame.
add_box(machine, "main base", (1.75, 4.6, .63), (LINE_X, 1.25, .42), (.53, .65, .64))
add_box(machine, "front base fascia", (1.74, .07, .48), (LINE_X, -1.02, .46), (.67, .76, .74))
for x in (LINE_X-.78, LINE_X+.78):
    for y in (-.95, .65, 2.45, 3.48):
        add_box(machine, "frame post %.2f %.2f" % (x, y), (.085, .085, 1.55),
                (x, y, 1.12), steel)
        add_box(machine, "foot %.2f %.2f" % (x, y), (.14, .14, .15), (x, y, .075), darksteel)
    add_box(machine, "lower long rail %.2f" % x, (.08, 4.55, .10), (x, 1.25, .81), steel)
    add_box(machine, "upper long rail %.2f" % x, (.07, 4.55, .07), (x, 1.25, 1.84), steel)
for y in (-.95, .65, 2.45, 3.48):
    add_box(machine, "upper cross rail %.2f" % y, (1.62, .07, .07),
            (LINE_X, y, 1.84), steel)

# Conveyor extends toward the camera through the machine.
belt_mid = (BELT_FRONT + BELT_BACK)/2
belt_len = BELT_BACK - BELT_FRONT
add_box(machine, "belt bed", (BELT_WIDTH, belt_len, .11), (LINE_X, belt_mid, BELT_Z-.06), darksteel)
add_box(machine, "pale conveyor belt", (BELT_WIDTH-.07, belt_len, .035),
        (LINE_X, belt_mid, BELT_Z+.01), belt)
for x in (LINE_X-.57, LINE_X+.57):
    add_box(machine, "conveyor edge rail %.2f" % x, (.065, belt_len+.1, .12),
            (x, belt_mid, BELT_Z+.045), steel)
    add_box(machine, "upper guide %.2f" % x, (.035, 4.7, .035),
            (x, 1.5, 1.19), steel)
    for y in (-.8, .5, 1.8, 3.1):
        add_rod(machine, "guide support %.2f %.2f" % (x, y),
                (x, y, .96), (x, y, 1.19), .018, darksteel)
# Low, pale waiting trays, spaced down the belt.
for i, y in enumerate((.05, .70, 1.35, 2.0, 2.65, 3.30)):
    add_box(machine, "product tray %02d" % i, (.65, .38, .035),
            (LINE_X, y, BELT_Z+.045), (.73, .83, .72))
    add_box(machine, "product insert %02d" % i, (.51, .27, .022),
            (LINE_X, y, BELT_Z+.075), (.70, .79, .61))

# Visible machine head: dark recess, shafts, crossbars, actuator array.
add_box(machine, "dark central machine head", (1.18, 1.15, .63),
        (LINE_X, 2.15, 1.46), (.10, .17, .17))
add_box(machine, "head top plate", (1.48, 1.23, .09),
        (LINE_X, 2.15, 1.81), steel)
add_box(machine, "head lower plate", (1.37, 1.0, .09),
        (LINE_X, 2.15, 1.17), steel)
for x in (LINE_X-.45, LINE_X-.15, LINE_X+.15, LINE_X+.45):
    add_rod(machine, "vertical pneumatic cylinder %.2f" % x,
            (x, 1.65, 1.32), (x, 1.65, 1.75), .055, steel)
    add_rod(machine, "actuator piston %.2f" % x,
            (x, 1.65, 1.10), (x, 1.65, 1.32), .023, (.68, .76, .74))
for z in (1.25, 1.45, 1.65):
    add_rod(machine, "transverse linkage %.2f" % z,
            (LINE_X-.61, 1.57, z), (LINE_X+.61, 1.57, z), .022, darksteel)
for y in (.0, .55, 2.95, 3.35):
    add_box(machine, "machine crosspiece %.2f" % y, (1.50, .07, .075),
            (LINE_X, y, 1.03), steel)
# Transparent guard sheets, split into panels with visible gaps and metal frames.
for side in (-1, 1):
    x = LINE_X + side*.79
    for j, (y0, y1) in enumerate(((-.9, .60), (.70, 2.40), (2.50, 3.43))):
        add_box(machine, "clear side guard %d %d" % (side, j),
                (.012, y1-y0, .86), (x, (y0+y1)/2, 1.37), glass, opacity=.17)
for y in (-.91, 3.43):
    add_box(machine, "clear end guard %.2f" % y, (1.51, .012, .84),
            (LINE_X, y, 1.38), glass, opacity=.15)
add_box(machine, "small nameplate", (.27, .015, .10), (LINE_X+.48, -1.065, .54), (.83, .88, .85))
add_box(machine, "nameplate line", (.16, .008, .012), (LINE_X+.48, -1.075, .55), darksteel)
# Small foreground uprights and end equipment visible at the right.
for x in (LINE_X+.88, LINE_X+1.25, LINE_X+1.62):
    add_box(machine, "foreground upright %.2f" % x, (.10, .12, .57), (x, -1.35, .75), steel)
    add_box(machine, "black cap %.2f" % x, (.12, .14, .055), (x, -1.35, 1.055), black)
scene.include("packaging machine", machine)

# A screen as a thin framed rectangle in a plane tilted toward the operator.
# Using a common tilt makes the layered panel and display remain aligned.
hmi = Asset("Articulated HMI")
add_rod(hmi, "vertical arm", (1.76, 1.20, 1.73), (1.76, 1.20, 2.23), .07, darksteel)
add_rod(hmi, "diagonal arm", (1.76, 1.20, 2.23), (1.40, .93, 2.43), .065, steel)
ellipsoid(hmi, "hinge", (1.76, 1.20, 2.23), (.11, .11, .11), darksteel)
# Screen faces camera/left; front is toward negative Y.
panel_center = (1.33, .88, 2.38)
panel = box((.78, .10, 1.10), center=panel_center, color=(.50, .62, .61))
panel.turn(axis="+y", degrees=18, pivot=panel_center)
hmi.include("metal screen frame", panel)
front_center = (1.33, .817, 2.38)
display = box((.64, .018, .94), center=front_center, color=screen)
display.turn(axis="+y", degrees=18, pivot=front_center)
hmi.include("luminous screen face", display)
scene.include("HMI and support", hmi)

# Simplified people: coherent coat silhouettes and visible reaching arms.
def person(name, x, y, scale=1.0, operating=False):
    p = Asset(name)
    def P(dx, dy, z):
        return (x+dx*scale, y+dy*scale, z*scale)
    def E(label, center, dims, color):
        ellipsoid(p, label, P(*center), tuple(v*scale for v in dims), color)
    def R(label, a, b, r, color):
        add_rod(p, label, P(*a), P(*b), r*scale, color)
    # legs and shoes
    for side in (-1, 1):
        E("trouser leg %d" % side, (side*.13, 0, .31), (.115, .14, .34), (.16, .22, .21))
        E("shoe %d" % side, (side*.13, -.055, .045), (.14, .22, .07), (.09, .14, .14))
    E("long coat", (0, 0, .93), (.34, .22, .64), (.90, .95, .93))
    E("shoulders", (0, 0, 1.38), (.34, .21, .22), (.91, .96, .94))
    E("neck", (0, 0, 1.59), (.10, .095, .13), skin)
    E("head", (0, 0, 1.77), (.145, .13, .21), skin)
    E("hairnet cap", (-.025, .015, 1.89), (.16, .145, .13), hairnet)
    # nose projects right in the image
    E("nose", (.14, -.025, 1.79), (.055, .045, .045), skin)
    if operating:
        R("raised upper sleeve", (.20, -.01, 1.43), (.48, -.05, 1.39), .105, (.91, .96, .94))
        R("raised forearm sleeve", (.48, -.05, 1.39), (.72, .02, 1.62), .085, (.90, .95, .93))
        E("touching hand", (.76, .03, 1.65), (.085, .055, .06), skin)
        R("lower sleeve", (-.20, 0, 1.37), (-.23, -.04, 1.02), .10, (.88, .94, .92))
    else:
        R("left sleeve", (-.23, 0, 1.37), (-.24, -.08, 1.04), .09, (.89, .95, .93))
        R("right sleeve", (.23, 0, 1.37), (.25, -.11, 1.06), .09, (.89, .95, .93))
        R("left bent arm", (-.24, -.08, 1.04), (.02, -.16, .99), .075, (.89, .95, .93))
        R("right bent arm", (.25, -.11, 1.06), (.08, -.17, .99), .075, (.89, .95, .93))
        E("hands", (.05, -.18, 1.0), (.11, .07, .07), skin)
        R("glasses bridge", (-.12, -.123, 1.80), (.12, -.123, 1.80), .012, darksteel)
    scene.include(name, p)

person("foreground operator", -.78, .15, 1.35, True)
person("background worker", -2.15, 2.30, 1.0, False)

realize(scene)

# Camera and render setup are applied after realization because it clears Blender.
set_view(CAMERA_POS, CAMERA_TARGET, lens=CAMERA_LENS, sensor=36)
sc = bpy.context.scene
sc.render.resolution_x = 1536
sc.render.resolution_y = 1023
sc.render.resolution_percentage = 100

if sc.world is None:
```
